# 06 `color` reaches the label text, in both kinds

> **Reissued.** The first attempt returned `blocked` without touching a file, for two reasons that
> were both the planner's: the write scope omitted the files that construct the types, and the
> ticket (following ADR-0008's amendment) specified a fix that does not work. Both are resolved
> below. The investigation that found them is preserved here rather than left to be repeated.

## Outcome

`classDef highlight fill:#111,color:#fff` darkens the box **and** lightens the text on it, in a
flowchart and in a class diagram, by one rule written once.

## Why this ticket exists

ADR-0008's amendment, landing. Today an author style reaches the frame alone, so `fill:#111` gives
a dark box with the theme's dark text on it, unreadable, and no directive fixes it. The failure is
not that the style was ignored — it was applied *halfway*. `color:` is what a Mermaid author
already writes to recolor a label, and Siren accepts the declaration today and silently paints it
onto a rect that has no text in it.

## The correction ADR-0008's amendment needs, and this ticket must make

The amendment says `color` "is emitted onto the class's `<text>` elements instead". **Taken
literally that ships the same bug one element over.** SVG text is painted by `fill`, not by
`color`; an inline `color` sits in a different property and never reaches it. Measured twice — by
the first worker, and independently by the integrator:

```
<text style="color:#fff">  computed fill = #1a1a2e   (the theme's, unchanged)   color = rgb(255,255,255)
<text style="fill:#fff">   computed fill = #ffffff   (the author's)
```

**So the routing is a translation, not a relabelling: the author writes `color`, and the text
bucket carries `fill`.** That is this board's domain decision 1 for the third time — an authored
spelling is normalized once and one vocabulary lives downstream, exactly as `TD` becomes `TB`,
`cssClass` becomes `apply`, and a `linkStyle` index becomes an edge id.

The rejected alternative is changing the theme to `fill: currentColor` so a `color` would inherit
down. It needs `theme/default.css`, and worse, it makes every text rule resolve through
inheritance — which is the precise mechanism ADR-0008's placement argument exists to avoid.

- [x] **`docs/adr/0008-...md`'s amendment is corrected** to say the text bucket carries `fill`
      translated from the author's `color`, and why emitting `color` verbatim would not work.
      Write it in the ADR's own voice, as its existing amendments are written.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `ResolvedStyle` carries the split already made — the properties bound for the frame and the
      properties bound for the label text — decided in `resolveStyles`, not in either renderer. Two
      renderers must not be able to disagree about what a text property is (board decision 3).
- [x] The author's `color` becomes `fill` in the text bucket. Assert the translation at the
      `resolveStyles` seam, not only through the DOM.
- [x] **`color` is the only text property.** Recorded reasoning from the first attempt, which you
      may adopt or challenge: `font-size`/`font-weight`/`font-family` are genuine text properties
      that Mermaid's `classDef` accepts, but `layoutClassDiagram` **measures text to size its
      boxes**, so an author changing the font would silently desynchronize the drawn text from the
      box computed for it — a layout ticket, not this one. `stroke` means the frame's border
      everywhere else in this codebase.
- [x] **Class diagram**: `color` reaches `siren-class-name`, `siren-member` and
      `siren-class-annotation`. Verified complete by the first attempt against
      `renderClassDiagramToSVG.ts` (lines 362, 380, 374, 391). `buildRelationshipText` (line 195)
      draws relationship labels and cardinalities, which no `style`/`classDef` targets — correctly
      excluded.
- [x] **Flowchart node**: `color` reaches the node's label `<text>`. Note it carries **no `class`
      attribute** — the theme reaches it by the descendant selector `.siren-node text` — and inline
      still wins, so **no new class is needed**. This differs from the class diagram's shape;
      do not add a `siren-node-label` class on the assumption that symmetry is wanted.
- [x] **Flowchart edge**: nothing to do, and pin it. An edge is one `<path class="siren-edge">`
      with no `<text>`, so `linkStyle 0 color:#f00` has no element to land on. `resolveStyles`
      should still route it into the text bucket — the rule stays kind-neutral, which is the whole
      design of that module — and the renderer simply has nowhere to apply it. **Assert that
      `color` on an edge does NOT end up on the `<path>`**, since that is the bug being fixed, one
      element over.
- [x] Everything that is not a text property still lands on the frame, unchanged. Assert a mixed
      declaration (`fill` and `color` in one `classDef`) splitting correctly in one test.
- [x] The validation gate sees text properties exactly as frame properties — `color:url(#evil)` is
      rejected the same way. Assert it.
- [x] **A real precedence assertion is available here** — the first attempt established it. Unlike
      ticket 02's specificity finding, jsdom *does* resolve inline style correctly, so you can
      assert computed `fill` rather than only which element carries the attribute. One caveat to
      write into the comment: `theme/default.test.ts:654` records that jsdom does not model
      `!important` at all, so jsdom over-prefers inline; the assertion is only sound because that
      same file separately asserts the theme contains no `!important`. Cite that pairing.

## Dropped criterion

The original asked you to update "existing class-diagram tests that assert `color` landing on the
frame". **There are none** — the first attempt searched every `.test.ts` under `packages/core/src`
and no test declares a `color:` author-style property at all. The criterion had no referent and is
removed rather than left to be hunted for.
